known.title: yolo Landing step 9 lets the Merge now answer confirm a production cleanup
known.summary: yolo Landing step 9 says that the `Merge now` answer confirms each production cleanup that the merge question names. The contract states the opposite: Production resources (plan-contract.md:441-445) says that a production cleanup needs an in-session `ask` immediately before it and that a yolo invocation does not answer that question, the Yolo runs table (plan-contract.md:472) gives a production cleanup its own question, and Checks and merge (plan-contract.md:350-354) lets the `Merge now` text confirm only remote non-production cleanups. yolo's own constraints (yolo/SKILL.md:35-36 and 44-45) and the plan-manager constraint (plan-manager/SKILL.md:30-34) also require a separate question. A yolo run that follows step 9 removes or undeploys a production resource without the question that the owner required (plan export, Decisions, Production bullet).

known.title: Run summary lists the merged local branch as kept after Merge now
known.summary: The run-summary reference tells the run to list `the merged local branch` under Kept resources after `Merge now`, in place of the resources that Teardown keeps. But Teardown deletes that branch with `git branch -d <branch>` after archive (plan-contract.md:417-419), the merge question states that delete (yolo/SKILL.md:298-299; plan-contract.md:350-354), and the contract's Kept resources lists only the resources that teardown keeps (plan-contract.md:449-451). So the pull request description and the final report name a deleted branch as kept, and they leave out a worktree or branch that git refused to remove. The plan (Decisions, Run summary bullet) says that the summary stops naming the merged local branch.

known.title: Teardown removes the plan worktree by its branch name
known.summary: After archive step 4 runs `git worktree remove -- <branch>`. git identifies a worktree by its path, or by the last path components of that path when they are unique, not by the branch that it holds (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree: "Worktrees can be identified by path, either relative or absolute. If the last path components in the worktree's path is unique among worktrees, it can be used to identify a worktree."). A yolo worktree is `agent-worktrees/<repository-name>/issue-<n>` and holds the branch that `gh issue develop` made (plan-contract.md:504-509), so the command stops with `fatal: '<branch>' is not a working tree` (git 2.53.0). The worktree stays, and step 6 `git branch -d` then also refuses, because the branch is still checked out in that worktree (plan export, Experiments table).

known.title: Teardown fast-forwards before it switches to the default branch
known.summary: After archive step 5 runs `git pull --ff-only origin <default>` and only then `git switch <default>`. In the user's checkout the plan branch is still the current branch (plan-contract.md:315-317, `gh issue develop ... --checkout`), and git pull integrates the fetched branch into the current branch (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull: "Integrate changes from a remote repository into the current branch."). So after a merge-commit landing the pull fast-forwards the plan branch to the remote default branch, and after a squash or rebase landing it fails; the switch then leaves the local default branch stale. Step 6 `git branch -d <branch>` then refuses with `not fully merged` (git 2.53.0), so the branch that the `Merge now` answer confirmed for deletion stays. The plan (Decisions, Order after archive) gives the correct order: switch, fast-forward, then `git branch -d`.
